subject.title: [Feature]: deterministic context injection for bootstrap files and session-type filtering

question: Should OpenClaw define a new core bootstrap-context contract for dynamic command expansion, session-type file selection, and live-time injection, or keep those requests on existing hooks/session_status and narrower PRs?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested shape adds public config semantics, changes prompt/session context, and introduces a command-execution boundary that needs maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Design One Bootstrap Contract
options.body: Sponsor a unified design for safe dynamic context, session-scoped selection, and cache-stable time behavior, then reconcile open subset PRs against that design.

options.title: Land Only Narrow Selection Subsets
options.body: Proceed with focused review of the tiered-bootstrap and exact-session PRs while explicitly deferring command expansion and live-clock injection.

options.title: Decline Command And Clock Injection
options.body: Keep bootstrap files static and cache-stable, steering dynamic context to hooks and current-time needs to session_status or message envelopes.

recommendation.title: Design One Bootstrap Contract
recommendation.body: Sponsor a unified design for safe dynamic context, session-scoped selection, and cache-stable time behavior, then reconcile open subset PRs against that design.

likelyOwner.reason: The original subagent bootstrap-context limit and related system-prompt/bootstrap history make this the strongest product/API routing signal.
